steps.title: Leave the windows up
steps.body: Keep the tinted windows closed so the film can bond to the glass.

steps.title: Windows down again
steps.body: You can use the windows normally now. Small water bubbles can take a couple of weeks to clear in cold weather.

steps.title: Clean the inside
steps.body: Clean the inside of the glass with a soft cloth and an ammonia-free cleaner. No blades or scrapers.

steps.title: Check the edges
steps.body: If an edge lifts or a bubble hasn't cleared, send us a photo and we'll fix it under warranty.

steps.title: No washing for now
steps.body: Keep the car out of washes and pressure washers while the film settles.

steps.title: First hand wash
steps.body: Hand wash with a pH-neutral shampoo. Keep a pressure washer at least 30cm from edges.

steps.title: Look at the edges
steps.body: Check corners and door edges. Anything lifting, message us and we'll book you in.

steps.title: Six-month check
steps.body: Pop in for a free look-over and a top-up of the wrap sealant.

steps.title: Leave it alone
steps.body: Small haze or water spots under the film are normal and clear as it dries.

steps.title: First wash
steps.body: Hand wash only, pH-neutral shampoo, no polish on the film.

steps.title: Haze gone?
steps.body: Any haze left after a month, send us a photo.

steps.title: Six-month check
steps.body: Free inspection of edges and a fresh coat of film sealant.

steps.title: Keep it dry
steps.body: Keep the car dry and out of the rain if you can; the coating is still curing.

steps.title: First wash
steps.body: Two-bucket hand wash with a pH-neutral shampoo. No automatic washes.

steps.title: Maintenance wash
steps.body: Book a maintenance wash so we can check the coating is beading.

steps.title: Yearly check
steps.body: Annual inspection to keep the 3-year cover valid.

questions.a: Rear windows can be any shade. The front side windows must let at least 70% of light through and the windscreen at least 75% (cars first used from 1 April 1985). We measure on your car after fitting and we don't fit darker on the front.

questions.q: Can I wait while you do it?
questions.a: Yes, for jobs up to about two hours, like rear tint on a hatch. The lounge has coffee and Wi-Fi. Wraps and PPF mean leaving the car with us.
For wraps, PPF and ceramic, yes: £50 to hold your day, taken off the bill. Tint and washes, no.
Tint: lifetime on the film and our fitting while you own the car. Wraps: 2 years on fitting. PPF: 5 years on the film. Full details are on our warranty page.

questions.q: How long does a wrap take?
questions.a: About four to five working days for a full wrap, depending on the car. Every job's time is on the prices page.
Drive into the yard and leave the car outside the roller door. Two customer spaces by the lounge.
PPF is thicker and made to take stone chips; most of it is clear, so your paint shows through. A wrap changes the colour and gives light protection. Coloured PPF does both.

questions.q: Can you film the grille, lights and badges?
questions.a: Yes. Grilles, headlights and rear lights are cut piece by piece. Badges stay on; we cut round them.

pages.description: Full and part wraps at Apex Studio, Birmingham: gloss, satin, matte and chrome, how long it takes and how to look after it.

blocks.heading: How it works
blocks.body:
We wash and decontaminate the car, take off badges, lights and handles where needed, and wrap every panel by hand, edges tucked.

A full wrap takes about four to five working days.

blocks.caption: Edges tucked by hand.

pages.title: Our *warranty.*
pages.description: What the Apex Studio warranty covers for tint, wraps, PPF and ceramic coating.
pages.intro: What's covered, for how long, and how to claim.

blocks.heading: How long
items: Window tint: film and fitting for as long as you own the car.
Wraps: two years on our fitting, plus the film maker's own warranty.
PPF: five years on the film, with a free six-month check.
Ceramic coating: three years with a yearly check.

blocks.heading: What isn't covered
blocks.body: Damage from accidents, stone chips through the film, scratches from automatic car washes, and wear from products we've asked you not to use.

blocks.text: Something not right? Send us a photo and we'll book you in.

tintPage.title: Window *tint.*
tintPage.intro: Every shade on a real window, inside and out, what's legal on each window, and what it costs for your car.
tintPage.message: Hi, can I ask about window tint?

steps.title: Check the glass
steps.body: We measure your factory glass first, so we know how dark a front film can go and still be legal.

steps.title: Clean and cut
steps.body: Each window is deep-cleaned and the film is cut to its exact shape.

steps.title: Fit
steps.body: The film goes on the inside of the glass and is pressed flat, edge to edge.

steps.title: Measure
steps.body: Before you collect, we measure the light through each front window and show you the reading.

steps.title: Aftercare
steps.body: Keep the windows up for four days. The steps can go straight into your calendar.

films.best: Most cars. It's the film we fit most.

films.name: Ceramic

films.best: Front windows, and anyone who drives a lot.

tintPage.filmsNote: We'll show you each film on glass at the studio before you choose.

windscreen.body: We fit clear heat-control film and light chameleon films to windscreens, and only after we've metered the bare glass. If the reading with the film on would be under 75%, we tell you and don't fit it.
points: Chameleon films change colour with the angle: violet, blue or green.
The reading on your car is what counts, not the number on the box.
One piece of film, cut to your screen, with no join across your view.

lights.body: We fit clear protection film to headlights, to stop stone chips and yellowing. We also fit light smoke film to rear lights, but not to headlights.
points: Clear headlight film keeps the beam as it is.
Rear smoke is a light shade, and we check every lamp with the lights on before you go.
Ask to see both on a lamp at the studio before you choose.
